title: dev: the Vite dev Console cannot import @objectstack/lint in the browser (node:module createRequire named import), so every in-browser lint caller silently degrades to no lint under `pnpm dev`
body:
domain:ui#3 · os-tesla · session_01L9qibz8HEj53Wx2uphTo2o

Filing gate: ① a named, reproduced defect, measured by the #28240 card thread on PR #28329's branch. It is not a card ask; that PR does not change it.

## Business reason

**Who:** anyone who develops or checks a lint-backed Studio/Console feature with the Vite dev server: the #28240 object picker closure, `preview/capabilityLint.ts`, `preview/securityPostureLint.ts`, `metadata-admin/celAuthoring.ts`. **What happens:** under the dev server, `import('@objectstack/lint')` throws in the browser. Every caller catches the error and degrades to "no lint, the server judges", so nothing on screen shows the failure. A developer either reads that as "the feature works" when it has done nothing, or has to rebuild production (`vite build` + `vite preview`) to see the feature at all. #28240 had to measure on the production bundle. **If not done:** each lint-backed authoring feature keeps a dev loop that cannot show it, and its regressions are invisible until someone does a production build.

## Reading (verbatim)

Browser console, Vite dev Console, at the picker's `import('@objectstack/lint')`:

```
Module "module" has been externalized for browser compatibility. Cannot access "module.createRequire" in client code.
```

Vite's log names the importer as the bundled dist and also externalizes `fs` and `path` from it:

```
[plugin rolldown:vite-resolve] Module "module" has been externalized for browser compatibility, imported by ".../packages/lint/dist/index.js"
```

The production rolldown build leaves an inert stub, so the bundle loads. This was measured on PR #28329's branch with `vite build` and `vite preview`.

## Mechanism

Six source files do `import { createRequire } from 'node:module'`:

- `packages/lint/src/validate-rule-compilability.ts:137`
- `packages/lint/src/validate-react-page-props.ts:36`
- `packages/lint/src/lint-liveness-properties.ts:30`
- `packages/lint/src/lint-startup-registry-verdict.ts:117`
- `packages/lint/src/validate-react-pages.ts:13`
- `packages/lint/src/validate-hook-body-writes.ts:89`

Each one already defers the `createRequire(...)` call into a function. The failure is the named import binding itself. When that binding is linked, Vite dev's browser-external stub throws on property access. The production build's stub does not. `./runtime` does not avoid the failure, because its graph is 70/71 shared with `.` (see the header of `packages/lint/src/runtime.ts`).

## Fix direction (owner decides the shape)

Two candidates, neither tried yet. (a) Use a namespace import that is read lazily (`import * as nodeModule from 'node:module'`, then `nodeModule.createRequire` inside the function), plus the same for `fs`/`path` if they throw too. (b) Add a `browser` export condition in `packages/lint/package.json` that resolves to a build without the node-only rules.

Prior ruling to respect: on #9707 (2026-08-18, comment 5335188168) the PM ruled that `packages/lint` needs **no** browser-safe entry. That ruling was about bundle weight in production, which objectui#5266 fixed with lazy chunking. This card is a dev-only load failure, which is a different defect. (a) does not add an entry. (b) does, so it would need that ruling revisited.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Under the Vite dev server, `await import('@objectstack/lint')` resolves in the browser (no `module.createRequire` error), measured in the dev Console.
- [ ] Node consumers (CLI compile, the server's runtime gate) behave the same: the existing `packages/lint` suite is green.
- [ ] The production build guard in `ui/apps/console/vite.config.ts` (lint stays out of the eager closure) still passes.

## Reader and dedupe

- **Who acts:** `domain:devx` (dev path). The edit lands in `packages/lint`.
- **Dedupe:** #9707 (closed, production bundle weight, related, does not cover dev). An open-issue search for vite/createRequire/externalized returned nothing.

Refs #28240 · Refs #28329 · Refs #9707
